sources.title: Introducing Fugu Max and Fugu Ultra v2
sources.evidence: Reopened in full October 27, 2026. September 11 announcement makes Max and Ultra v2 available that day and describes the same core orchestration architecture optimized for different objectives. It names an expanded pool including the Nemotron family, but no Max backbone, nominal total, or active count. The opening multi-trillion-parameter example is a general argument about inefficient deployment, not a Fugu specification. Benchmark figures compare task scores, prices and cost-performance, not activated parameters.

sources.title: Sakana API model and capability documentation
sources.evidence: Reopened October 27, 2026. Maps fugu-max to fugu-max-v1.0 and describes its fixed worker pool, distinct from the configurable default Fugu pool. Current comparison section provides task scores and prices, but no total or activated-parameter column or named Max base checkpoint. Documents caller-defined functions, model-invoked internal web tools with returned tool items, and text/structured-text output contracts.

sources.title: Pinned official Fugu client model catalog
sources.evidence: Reopened pinned original October 27, 2026. Exact fugu-max entry gives context_window=1000000, text/image input, high/xhigh reasoning, freeform apply_patch and parallel tool calls. This is a client/service configuration; no neural backbone dimensions, checkpoint identity, total or active counts are specified.

sources.title: Sakana API getting started
sources.evidence: Confirms the exact Max configuration and high/xhigh effort support; max is accepted as an alias of xhigh. Reasoning summaries are not supported for Max, which does not negate reasoning capability.

sources.title: Sakana AI API Platform Terms of Service
sources.evidence: Current API terms cover Fugu and reserve service/configuration intellectual-property rights to Sakana and its licensors, granting only limited service use. This supports proprietary hosted-service classification, not an open model-weight grant.

sources.title: Sakana Fugu Technical Report, June 23 revision
sources.evidence: Reopened full June 23 v2 report October 27, 2026, including architecture/training sections and comparison tables. Covers June Fugu and Fugu-Ultra, not September Max. Section 3.1 attaches a selection head and adapts singular-value scales; section 3.2 scales Conductor from an unnamed pretrained language model. Table 1 and other comparisons report task performance, not total/active counts. The framework relationship does not identify Max as an unchanged named checkpoint.

sources.title: Testing a Gemma 4 based Fugu orchestrator
sources.evidence: Reopened complete August 10 article October 27, 2026. Earlier Fugu orchestrators were Qwen-based without an exact named checkpoint; the article tests a separately trained Gemma 4 E2B orchestrator to demonstrate backbone interchangeability. It separates the small orchestrator from the worker pool. It predates Max and supplies no statement assigning either base to Max, so neither the experimental E2B designation nor worker sizes establish a Max count.

sources.title: Sakana Chat Update: Fugu Max for Everyone, Now with Memory
sources.evidence: Direct retry returned HTTP 200 October 27, 2026 at 17:46 UTC after an earlier 503. Full Japanese and English September 17 article confirms that the already API-available Max becomes the Sakana Chat orchestrator, routing prompts across diverse open models. It names no backbone or total/active count; application memory and image/document attachments do not establish a neural parameter specification.

sources.title: Official Fugu repository inventory at pinned revision
sources.evidence: Complete nontruncated tree inspected: integration scripts, client configuration, research paper, examples and demonstrations; no Fugu Max checkpoint or neural model configuration. Repository README explicitly says its evaluations describe June models, while coordinators and pools are updated over time.

sources.title: SakanaAI public Hugging Face model inventory
sources.evidence: Official organization model inventory contained no Fugu or Fugu Max weights. Negative inventory evidence supplements the explicit API distribution, rather than proving nonexistence alone.

sources.title: Exact Fugu Max provider metadata
sources.evidence: Sakana-hosted fugu-max-20260911 endpoint advertises context1000000, text/image/file input and text output, with reasoning and tools. Its created timestamp is a provider listing, not the original launch source. File is an API container type, not evidence for a separate PDF neural modality.

sources.title: Learning to Orchestrate Agents in Natural Language with the Conductor, v2
sources.evidence: Fetched and read October 27, 2026. Section 4.1 describes a 7B Conductor from a Qwen2.5 checkpoint; Appendix A names Qwen2.5-7B. Comparison tables report accuracy, tokens and cost. The text does not identify Fugu Max or establish that its orchestration backbone is this checkpoint; the nominal research count therefore cannot be transferred to Max.

sources.title: Recursive Self-Improvement through Multi-Agent Self-Supervision
sources.publisher: Sakana AI / UC Berkeley research team
sources.evidence: Fetched and read October 27, 2026 as later original research. Section 4.1 names Qwen3.6-27B-FP8 as the base shared by MASS agents, evaluator and optimizer; Figure 2 compares that base and its two self-improvement cycles. Full-text/table inspection finds no Max comparison or explicit active-parameter convention. The Fugu technical report appears as related research, not a statement that Max uses the MASS checkpoint.

name.note: Official exact variant name; current API version is fugu-max-v1.0.

developer.note: Developer and operator of the orchestrator system, distinct from the worker-model developers.

family.note: Lowercase catalog family for the Fugu orchestrator products.

release_date.note: Explicit API availability on September 11. September 17 is the later Chat rollout; original Fugu beta/GA dates do not date Max.

open_weights.note: Released as a proprietary hosted API. Open-weight workers do not constitute release of the Max orchestrator/system weights; no Max checkpoint was found in the checked official inventories.

license.note: Classification of the Max service; do not inherit licenses of worker models, research papers or example code.

parameters_b.note: Fresh October 27 primary-source review and bounded searches for exact Fugu Max/fugu-max-v1.0 parameter counts and Qwen/Gemma base lineage found no published nominal total or named unchanged base for Max. Same core orchestration architecture as Ultra v2 does not identify a checkpoint. The Conductor Qwen2.5-7B, experimental Gemma 4 E2B and later MASS Qwen3.6-27B-FP8 counts belong to other identified research systems. This null reflects missing Max identity/count evidence, not a demand for an exact tensor census. Worker-pool counts and the generic multi-trillion example cannot be summed or relabeled as Max parameters.

active_parameters_b.note: Separately rechecked October 27 using exact Max active/activated-parameter and model-size searches, current official benchmark comparisons, the Fugu/Conductor reports and later MASS research tables. No exact Max row establishes a nominal active-count convention, and no named backbone lineage supports transferring one. A pool of externally invoked models does not define neural expert activation; agent counts, token budgets, worker parameter sums and total-equals-active assumptions are not active-parameter evidence.

architecture.note: Learned model orchestration is disclosed at system level. Exact Max backbone and its dense/MoE/hybrid neural topology are not. Sharing a core orchestration design with Ultra v2 does not specify a shared checkpoint or make this a neural MoE. Earlier Qwen/Gemma research does not bind Max to a particular model.

context_window.note: Exact advertised service/client limit for fugu-max. This does not establish the native training window of the undisclosed orchestrator or every worker.

modalities.note: Exact official input list and text response contract. Remove PDF as a separate neural modality: document/file acceptance is an application/API capability. These are system-level capabilities, not proof that the small orchestrator itself has a vision encoder.

reasoning.note: Official Max effort controls high/xhigh verify reasoning support; max aliases xhigh. Lack of reasoning summaries is a separate output-interface restriction.

tool_call.note: Exact Max integration enables parallel caller tools; model documentation also explains Max choosing internal web tools and returning their items. This is more than deterministic retrieval or external software simply invoking Max.

description.value: Model orchestration system that selects and coordinates a fixed pool of open-weight and specialized models for each task.
description.note: Replaces vague expert-agent wording with the documented task-dependent system and fixed worker pool; makes no unsupported benchmark superiority claim.

patch.description: Model orchestration system that selects and coordinates a fixed pool of open-weight and specialized models for each task.
patch.notes: Fugu Max (API version fugu-max-v1.0) is a learned orchestration system with a fixed worker pool. Its total and active parameter counts and neural topology are undisclosed; published research checkpoints do not identify its backbone. The 1,000,000-token context and text/image input describe the service; document/file support is not a separate neural modality. Max supports high/xhigh reasoning and model-selected tools. September 11, 2026 is API availability; September 17 is the later Sakana Chat rollout.

summary: October 27 parameter re-audit retains explicit null total and active counts with parameters_source null. Reopened the Max launch, current docs, pinned client config, Fugu report, Gemma experiment and Chat announcement; checked Conductor lineage, later MASS research tables and fresh exact-model searches. No nominal Max count, unchanged named base or attributed active-count convention was found. Conductor 7B, Gemma 4 E2B and MASS 27B identify separate research systems. The other 12 field assessments are unchanged.
